model: Regulated utility dividend discount at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: Not deducted separately: the modelled stream is core earnings to common, which is already after stock-based compensation expense ($57M cash-flow add-back in FY2025, XBRL; $21M equity-statement line, 10-K FY2025 line 6100). Deducting it again would double-count.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-09-30 (387M weighted diluted, Q3-2026 10-Q EPS note; 385M weighted basic; 384.8M outstanding at 2026-10-22 cover page)
inputs.share_count_basis: 387M weighted diluted from the Q3-2026 10-Q dilutive-securities table. Held FLAT in base and bull: management's financing plan assumes no new common equity through 2030, and SBC is inside core earnings. In the bear case the equity issuance needed to fund an Eaton Fire disallowance is NOT modelled in the count; it is carried in the flows as a per-share earnings rebase (the growth path is a per-share path), so compounding the count as well would charge it twice.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest dividends. Built in USD: 10-year US Treasury 5.15% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-13) + beta 0.7 x 5.0% equity risk premium = 8.65%, rounded up to 8.75%. Beta 0.7 rather than the 0.6 used for a diversified multi-state utility (DUK, 8.25%) because EIX is a single-state, single-regulator utility whose equity has traded with a higher market beta since 2018. Same rate in all three scenarios: the Eaton Fire outcome, the legislative outcome and the wildfire-fund depletion risk are carried in the flows and the weights, not in the rate. Cross-check: the CPUC allows SCE roughly 10.1-10.6% ROE.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable on this route: lease cost and lease interest are inside net income, and no debt of any kind is deducted in the bridge. Lease liabilities $839M + $316M at FY2025.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: core earnings are available to Edison International common shareholders, after SCE preference stock dividends ($1,564M preference stock in NCI at 2026-09-30) and EIX Series B preferred dividends ($83M remaining after the Q1-2026 Series A redemption). Nothing further is deducted in the bridge.
inputs.bvps_memo: Common book value per share about $46.27 at 2026-09-30 ((19,453 total equity - 1,564 SCE preference stock - 83 EIX preferred) / 384.8M). FY2026E core ROE on that book about 13%, flattered by holdco leverage.
inputs.wildfire_treatment: No wildfire item sits in the equity bridge. The Eaton Fire exposure is scenario-dependent, so it is charged once, in the bear flows: SCE's reimbursement obligation to the Wildfire Fund is capped at about $4.3bn if the CPUC finds imprudence (Q3-2026 10-Q), about $11 per share pre-tax, absent a finding of conscious or willful disregard. At 2026-09-30 SCE had recorded $1.8bn of Eaton settlements against $917M self-insurance, $859M Wildfire Fund and $70M FERC recoveries, a net after-tax charge of $9M; management cannot estimate a range for the remaining loss.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. Edison International is a rate-regulated electric utility holdco (Southern California Edison, CPUC and FERC). The dcf-methods routing table has no utility row, so this was routed on its stated principle -- discount the flow the business actually produces, at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues -- and matches the method used for DUK. An owner-FCF DCF does not work here: reported FCF has been negative in 17 of the last 19 fiscal years (FY2025 -$715M; OCF $5,800M against capex $6,515M) because a utility's capex is rate-base growth it is allowed to earn on, funded with new debt rather than from operating cash flow. Discounting negative interim flows and then subtracting $41.6bn of debt gives a meaningless number. What an owner receives is the dividend, and what grows it is allowed-ROE earnings on a growing rate base. ENGINE MAPPING: base_revenue = FY2026E core earnings to common ($6.05 guidance midpoint x 385M basic shares = $2,329M; nine-month core earnings were $1,880M); growth_rates = core EPS growth; ebitda_margin_path = dividend payout ratio on EIX core earnings; SBC, D&A, capex, tax and working capital are zero because the stream is already after all of them; net_debt = 0 because the flow is post-interest (total_debt and cash are memo only). last_fcf = the 2026 common dividend ($0.8775 quarterly, $3.51 annualised x 385M = $1,351M), a 58% payout on EIX core EPS; the company's stated 45-55% target is on SCE core earnings, which are higher than EIX's by the holdco drag. GAAP FY2025 EPS of $11.55 is not a base: it includes large non-core gains from wildfire settlement-agreement recoveries (TKM and Woolsey) and is why trailing EPS CAGRs are unusable. Buyback cash ($42M in 9M-2026) is small and offsets employee awards. House and street bases coincide because SBC is not a separate driver. The price is a regular-session close.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (3.8%, FY2020 15,949 to FY2025 19,259, total equity) is about half the revenue 5-year CAGR (7.3%); wildfire charges in 2020-2024 suppressed retained earnings. The forward path is anchored to management's guided 5-7% core EPS growth and about 7% rate-base growth rather than to the book-value CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs are omitted: GAAP EPS runs 1.98 (FY2020), 1.60 (FY2022), 11.55 (FY2025), the last inflated by non-core wildfire-recovery gains, so the computed 3-year (93%) and 5-year (42%) rates are meaningless. FCF CAGRs are omitted because reported FCF is negative at both ends of each window. Core EPS, the usable series, has grown at mid-single digits.

base.narrative: Growth is core EPS growth; margin is dividend payout. EPS follows the guided midpoints ($6.45 for 2027, about $6.94 for 2028), then 5-7% to 2030, fading to 3.5%. Payout holds near 56-57% while the capital plan is funded without new equity, then rises to 65% as rate-base growth slows.

bull.narrative: EPS at the top of the guided ranges through 2028, then upper end of 5-7% as AMI 2.0 and the next GRC cycle lift rate-base growth; same payout path as base.

bear.narrative: Core EPS per share rebased about 19% over 2028-2029 as an Eaton Fire disallowance near the $4.3bn cap is funded with dilutive equity and holdco debt, then 3% growth; the dividend is cut to a 55% payout on the lower base.

scenario_narratives.base: The AB 1054 framework works roughly as written. SCE held a valid safety certification at the time of the Eaton Fire, the presumption of prudence largely holds, and losses above the exhausted $1.0bn self-insurance layer are reimbursed by the Wildfire Fund without a material shareholder disallowance. Core EPS tracks management's guided midpoints (2026 $5.90-6.20, 2027 $6.25-6.65, 2028 $6.74-7.14) on about 7% rate-base growth and a $38-41bn 2026-2030 capital plan funded without new common equity. Growth fades to 3.5% as the hardening programme matures and affordability pressure caps capex; payout drifts up to 65%. No legislative reform is assumed, and none is needed for this path.
scenario_narratives.bull: Durable wildfire-liability reform passes in a 2027 session or special session, the CPUC issues a first prudency decision that validates the AB 1054 standard, and the Eaton Fire is resolved inside the fund. Credit outlooks stabilise, financing costs fall, and core EPS runs at the top of the guided range with rate-base growth accelerating after 2028 on AMI 2.0, electrification load and transmission build-out. The dividend grows with earnings.
scenario_narratives.bear: The CPUC finds SCE's ignition-related conduct at the idle Eaton Canyon transmission tower imprudent and SCE must reimburse the Wildfire Fund up to the roughly $4.3bn liability cap. With no reform enacted, the fund is materially depleted by Eaton claims, S&P (BBB-, negative outlook) and Fitch (negative outlook) move the holdco to the edge of investment grade, and the no-equity financing plan breaks: equity is issued at a depressed price and the dividend is cut. Core EPS per share is rebased about 19% over two years and then grows only 3% as affordability politics trim the capital plan and allowed returns. This is not the worst outcome: a finding of conscious or willful disregard removes the cap, and a second catastrophic fire against a depleted fund is not in any of the three paths.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 35%, well above the 15% house default: investigators have attributed the Eaton Fire to SCE equipment, the reform bill (SB 492) collapsed in September 2026, no CPUC decision has yet applied the AB 1054 prudency standard, and the whole equity case depends on one state's regulator and legislature. Base 45%: it is management's guided path and rests on a statutory presumption of prudence that SCE qualifies for, but that presumption is untested. Bull 20%, below the 35% default: it needs legislation that has just failed once AND a favourable prudency ruling AND an accelerated capital plan.

valuation_philosophy.summary: EIX is valued as what it is to an owner: a dividend stream growing with allowed-ROE earnings on a regulated rate base, discounted at a cost of equity. Free cash flow is structurally negative and debt is operating funding for rate base, so neither enters the valuation. The spread between scenarios is almost entirely the Eaton Fire prudency outcome and whether California's wildfire-liability regime holds; the rate-base growth itself is the least uncertain input.
key_risks_to_valuation: Eaton Fire: a CPUC imprudence finding costs up to about $4.3bn (about $11 per share pre-tax); a conscious-or-willful-disregard finding removes the cap and is outside all three scenarios
Wildfire Fund depletion: Eaton claims may consume a large share of the roughly $21bn fund, leaving a thinner backstop for the next fire under inverse condemnation
No legislative reform after SB 492's collapse; each session is a binary headline event
Credit: S&P BBB- with negative outlook, Fitch negative outlook; a holdco downgrade raises financing costs on $41.6bn of debt and could force equity issuance
Rate sensitivity: a 5%-plus ten-year Treasury; each 1pp on the cost of equity moves the base value by roughly 15%
Terminal value is the majority of the base value and depends on payout rising to 65% as growth slows
